writeAccessPicker.title: Enable write access
writeAccessPicker.description: Choose the {provider} account to authorize for write access on {sourceName}.
writeAccessPicker.loadFailed: Mailven couldn't load your accounts. Close this window and try again.
writeAccessPicker.emptyHint: Add a {provider} account in Mail (Settings → Accounts) or Contacts (Settings → Contacts → Add source) first, then return here.
writeAccessPicker.failureToast: Mailven couldn't turn on write access. Try again.

oauth.savedOverrideHint: You also have a saved Custom override — switch to Custom to use it.

sentPolicy.title: Sent copy policy
sentPolicy.guidance: Choose where a copy of each message you send is kept. Some providers save a copy in Sent automatically; otherwise Mailven can save one itself. If both do, you get two copies, so check your provider's settings before choosing. You can add more than one folder.
sentPolicy.unreviewed: Not set up yet. Mailven won't save copies itself, and tells you when it can't find a copy of a sent message.
sentPolicy.evidenceGuidance: Mailven looks for each sent message in these folders among the mail it has already synced, so a copy can show up late. If saving a copy is interrupted, Mailven doesn't try again on its own. A copy in Sent doesn't mean the message was delivered.

state.unknown: Saving the copy may not have finished; check the folder before copying the message yourself
state.appended: Copy saved; waiting for it to sync

mailApi.title: Mail API route
mailApi.intro: Optionally move this account from IMAP / SMTP to its provider’s mail API. Nothing changes until you confirm, and you can return to IMAP / SMTP afterwards.
mailApi.scopes: Authorization asks the provider for permission to read, change and send mail for this account only. It is separate from your current sign-in and can be removed here.
mailApi.limits: Limits: no route promises delivery or inbox placement. Shared mailboxes stay on IMAP / SMTP until their Graph checks are recorded, some provider limits (message size, Bcc handling) are not verified against the live service, and moving messages between accounts is not available on the API route.
mailApi.sharedNote: This shared mailbox uses your parent account’s work or school sign-in. It needs the Shared mail permissions and an administrator-granted delegation (Full Access to read, Send As or Send on Behalf to send). Migration stays unavailable until those live checks are recorded.
mailApi.authorized: API access is authorized. The account still uses IMAP / SMTP.
mailApi.reauthorize: The API authorization needs to be renewed. Authorize again to continue.
mailApi.partialConsent: Some requested permissions were not granted. Authorize again and accept all of them.
mailApi.counts: {folders} folders, {imap} IMAP messages, {api} API messages, {drafts} drafts, {queued} queued submissions, {pending} pending actions.
mailApi.blockers: Migration is blocked until these are resolved:
mailApi.consent: I understand that this account will use its mail API. Existing messages are matched by Message-ID and kept; drafts and queued mail are preserved; there is no automatic fallback between routes.
mailApi.snapshotNote: A snapshot of the local database is saved before anything changes.
mailApi.migrating: Migrating… this can take a while for large mailboxes.
mailApi.migrateFailed: Migration failed and the account stays on IMAP / SMTP: {error}
mailApi.resumeNote: A previous migration was interrupted. Migrating again resumes it.
mailApi.active: This account uses its mail API.
mailApi.rollbackConfirm: Return this account to IMAP / SMTP? Nothing is replayed to the provider. Actions still queued for the API stay queued and are listed afterwards.
mailApi.rolledBackSyncRequested: Returned to IMAP / SMTP. {applied} API actions were applied since migration. A background sync was requested; its completion is not confirmed.
mailApi.rolledBackSyncNotRequested: Returned to IMAP / SMTP. {applied} API actions were applied since migration. A sync was not requested; use Sync manually.
mailApi.unfinished: Actions that did not finish on the API route:

setupDiagnostic.title: Check account setup
setupDiagnostic.guidance: Checks that Mailven can connect securely and sign in with this address and the saved server settings. It sends no mail, and a successful sign-in doesn't prove that you may send from this address or that mail will be delivered. Nothing runs until you start it, and it never retries or asks for new permissions on its own; to sign in again, use the account's reauthorize option. The exported report leaves out email addresses and passwords.
setupDiagnostic.existingRoute: Your saved server settings for receiving (IMAP) and sending (SMTP) mail
setupDiagnostic.owned: Also check DNS records for a domain I own
setupDiagnostic.selectors: DKIM selectors supplied by your provider (comma separated, optional; maximum 10)
setupDiagnostic.failed: Could not start the diagnostic. Confirm the saved account, From identity and server hostnames, then retry.
setupDiagnostic.cancelFailed: Could not cancel the diagnostic. It will stop at its time limit.
setupDiagnostic.exportFailed: Could not export the report. Run the diagnostic again and retry.

sending.ok: Mailven connected securely and signed in.
sending.problem: Something failed. Open Details to see which step.
sending.unconfirmed: Mailven couldn't confirm every step. Open Details for what was missing.

dns.problem: A record is missing or invalid. Open Details to see which.
dns.unconfirmed: A lookup couldn't be completed. Open Details for which.
dns.notChecked: Not checked. Tick the domain option to check them.

permissions.ok: The saved sign-in includes the permissions needed.
permissions.problem: The saved sign-in lacks a permission. Re-authorize the account to grant it.
permissions.unconfirmed: Your provider decides whether you may send from this address; Mailven couldn't confirm it.

snapshotRestore.intro: This returns the whole database, every account, to the snapshot taken {date}. Mail, drafts, settings and local changes made after that are discarded from the database. Mailven closes to do this and must be reopened by you.
snapshotRestore.addedSince: Accounts added since the snapshot will be removed from Mailven: {emails}. Their saved passwords stay in your system keyring until you clean them up afterwards.
snapshotRestore.removedSince: Accounts removed since the snapshot come back: {emails}.
snapshotRestore.serverNote: Changes already made at your mail provider are not undone. The server stays as it is, and Mailven syncs from it again afterwards.
snapshotRestore.heldNote: Outgoing mail and API actions still queued are not sent after the restore. They are held and listed for your review.
snapshotRestore.backup: A backup of the current database is saved first in {dir}. You can undo the restore from it.
snapshotRestore.ack: I understand that local changes after {date} are discarded.
snapshotRestore.closing: Mailven is closing. Reopen it to finish the restore.
snapshotRestore.bannerRestored: Database restored to the snapshot from {date}.
snapshotRestore.bannerUndone: Restore undone. The database is back as it was before the restore.
snapshotRestore.bannerFailed: The database restore did not complete: {error}. Your database was not changed.
snapshotRestore.bannerDiscarded: A pending database restore could not be read and was set aside. Your database was not changed.
snapshotRestore.held: {count} queued API actions are held, not sent.
snapshotRestore.submissions: {count} queued outgoing messages were not sent automatically. Review them before sending.
snapshotRestore.routeNote: Mail API routes are inactive after a restore. Turn them on again in each account’s settings.
snapshotRestore.orphans: Saved credentials remain for accounts no longer in Mailven: {emails}.
snapshotRestore.undoIntro: Undo returns the database to how it was just before the restore, discarding anything done since. Mailven closes and must be reopened.
snapshotRestore.undoAck: I understand that changes since the restore are discarded.

googleGuide.help: Set up your own Google Cloud client with this checklist. It takes a few minutes and no command line.
googleGuide.copyFailed: Could not copy to the clipboard

project.title: Create a project
project.body: Create a new Google Cloud project, or pick an existing one. Keep it selected for the next steps.

apis.title: Enable the APIs
apis.body: Enable the Gmail, People and Calendar APIs together. Gmail API is needed for every Google account, even on IMAP.

branding.title: Set up branding
branding.body: Enter an app name such as Mailven and your email address as the support and contact address.

audience.title: Choose the audience
audience.body: Pick External. While the app is in Testing, add your Google address under Test users: only listed users can sign in, and sign-ins expire after 7 days. Publish the app to remove the expiry; Google then shows a warning screen for unverified apps, and personal use by a few users you know is exempt from verification.

scopes.title: Add the data access scopes
scopes.body: Open Data Access and choose Add or remove scopes. Copy the scopes below, paste them into Manually add scopes at the bottom of the panel, choose Add to table, then Update and Save.

clients.title: Create a Desktop app client
clients.body: Create a client of type Desktop app and download its JSON now. Google shows the client secret only once.

import.title: Import the JSON
import.body: Choose Import JSON… below this checklist, or paste the Client ID and Secret into Google Mail.
import.bodyInline: Choose Import JSON… and pick the file you downloaded. Sign in with Google then uses your client.

signin.title: Sign in and check
signin.body: Sign in with your Google account, then open the account's Identity settings and press Check Google setup.
